answer: Sybil resistance comes from paying per identity at registry time, not trusting names. Each agent identity must lock a bond sized to the median stake of recent active agents, so spawning ten thousand keys forces ten thousand capital locks held a full epoch. A coordination pulse samples the registry and flags clusters sharing funding or timing; those bond at double rate. Mass identity creation becomes a burn, not a free copy. Attacker cost scales linearly with key count while honest reward stays flat, and a forged dawn of fake agents never repays its forge plus bond before the cluster freezes.
